summary: Commit-window race during scheduled model upgrade causes tenant to be routed to fallback variant
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled model minor-version upgrade in the customer's Dedicated pool, a narrow race in the rollout commit window caused the tenant's session tokens to be routed to a fallback (smaller-quant) variant rather than the pinned primary model. Impact: Intermittent mixed-model responses (some requests returned quantized outputs with subtle tokenization differences) for a subset of BrightForms tenant traffic for ~8 minutes. No data leak; correctness impact limited to degraded generation quality and increased tokenization mismatches.

Background: BrightForms has a pinned model version for their route. We initiated a scheduled minor upgrade on 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC that touched the rollout-manager commit path and the router's pin cache TTL. During commit, some session leases were truncated by a retry path which cleared pin metadata before the router could persist the new pin. The router then fell back to its fallback mapping (quantized variant) for those sessions until the pin reconciler repaired state.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool with a pinned model version and a fallback quantized variant
Start sustained session traffic with session-lease extension enabled and a median latency of 70ms
Trigger a scheduled minor upgrade which performs a commit across rollout-manager and router within the same 30s window
Introduce an artificial retry on the rollout commit (simulate transient DB timeout) that runs commit twice with truncated lease metadata
Observe that some sessions lose their pin and are routed to the fallback variant until the reconciler runs
logs: 2026-03-10T02:05:11Z rollout-manager INFO commit start rollout_id=rl-7784 tenant=brightforms
2026-03-10T02:05:11Z router WARN session-lease truncate session=tok_3h2a flags=retry-path
2026-03-10T02:05:12Z rollout-manager ERROR commit retry due to transient-db-timeout: write failed (code=504)
2026-03-10T02:05:14Z router INFO route-evaluate tenant=brightforms resolved_variants=[quantized:0.0, primary:0.0] (fallback applied)
2026-03-10T02:13:21Z pin-reconciler INFO repaired 142 sessions for tenant=brightforms duration=00:08:07
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Commit retried while router persisted a partial state resulting in pin key being cleared on edge caches
Hypothesis 2: Session-lease truncation on retry path emitted an empty affinity token which bypassed pin-resolution heuristics
Finding: Correlated errors in rollout-manager (transient DB 504) with router session-truncate events. Reconciler timestamps align with the time window where mixed responses were observed.
Edge-proxy TTL configuration allowed stale negative cache entries for up to 45s which extended the window where fallback mapping was used after the transient error
Customer traffic pattern (highly-sustained with long sessions and lease extensions) increased probability of hitting the retry path during the commit window
comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Initial report from BrightForms: 'We saw weird shorter outputs and tokenization edge cases starting at 02:05 UTC for about 8 minutes. Many requests appeared to come from the same session ids.'
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged and started trace collection. Observed rollout-manager commit retries and router session-lease truncates. Marked as P1 given tenant production impact.

Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Notified customer of investigation and provided temporary mitigation: avoid scheduling upgrades during BrightForms heavy usage windows and to use shorter lease-extension TTLs as a stop-gap.
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-11: Reproducer run in staging with injected retry confirmed race. Created PR to add idempotent commit semantics to prevent lease truncation on commit retry. See PR #4212.

Product (Ava Chen) 2026-03-12: Requesting a follow-up to add an observability alert for 'pin-loss-rate' during rollouts and to reduce edge negative-cache TTL to 10s for dedicated pools as a protective default.
workaround: Short-term: Disable long session-lease auto-extension for the affected tenant and schedule upgrades during low-traffic windows. Operational: manual reconcilation (pin-reconciler) run completed which repaired sessions. Applied edge negative-cache TTL patch at the edge-proxy config level for the dedicated pool to 10s.
resolution: In progress: hotfix merged to rollout-manager to make commit idempotent and preserve lease metadata on retry (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-manager/pull/4212). Edge negative-cache TTL lowered for dedicated pools (router PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/3051). Pin-reconciler run repaired affected sessions; monitoring added to alert on 'session-pin-loss-rate'>0.5% during rollouts. Scheduled follow-up: make reconciler aggressive for first 5 minutes post-commit and add a canary-runner test that injects commit failures during staged upgrades.
next_steps: Ship rollout-manager idempotent-commit to production (canary scope: 5% of dedicated upgrades) - responsible: Diego Ramirez - target: 2026-03-16
Add alert for session-pin-loss-rate and a dashboard panel - responsible: Observability team - target: 2026-03-15
Update runbook to recommend edge negative-cache TTL <=10s for dedicated customers with long session leases - responsible: Product Ops - target: 2026-03-18
